title: KV-lease coordinator + batch-deflation protocol for graceful OOM reconstruction
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem statement: Recent incident INC-2026-02-05 exposed a class of tail OOMs during high-concurrency small-sequence workloads. Root cause analysis shows that aggressive continuous batching plus indiscriminate KV retention caused memory pressure spikes when multiple hot prefixes consolidated on the same GPU. Existing eviction policies (LRU-like compaction and host spill) are reactive and cause 2–4s tail latency spikes or failed requests when the runtime tries to reclaim memory under pressure.
goal: Design and implement a coordinated "KV-lease" mechanism and a batch-deflation admission controller that together reduce sudden memory pressure during peak admission and enable graceful reconstruction of state after partial eviction. The feature should: 1) provide short, soft leases for critical KV entries to avoid premature eviction for in-flight conversations; 2) shrink batch admission windows proactively under memory pressure to avoid OOMs; 3) support prioritized reconstruction (replay) of leased KV entries from client-side checkpoints, with retries and backoff; 4) be observable and toggleable per-customer and per-worker for safe rollout.
proposal_summary: Introduce a KV-lease coordinator inside the runtime memory manager: when a request inserts or pins KV state for a prefix, it acquires a 500–1500ms soft lease (configurable). Leases prevent eviction but are revocable by the coordinator under critical pressure. The admission controller monitors a moving memory pressure score and performs 'batch-deflation' — shrinking max batch size and tightening admission windows for new requests (shorter batching delay, smaller token cap). Add a reconstruction pipeline that, on lease revocation, marks KV as 'reconstructable' and triggers a prioritized sequence of: 1) client checkpoint rehydration (if available), 2) lightweight prefix re-prefetch (hot path), 3) fallback to a smaller model shard (micro-model) for degraded generation while reconstruction completes.
tradeoffs_and_notes:
- Pros: reduces hard OOMs, preserves latency for active conversations, enables deterministic fallback behavior.
- Cons: additional metadata and coordination overhead (leases), potential increased client complexity for checkpointing, possible minor increase in steady-state memory due to leased reservations.
- Risk: incorrect lease revocation thresholds can increase GC churn; batch-deflation tuning needs workload-specific defaults.
- Security/Compliance: KV-lease metadata contains no user PII; reconstruction fetches must honor tenant encryption/KMS policies.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype KV-lease coordinator and a toggleable admission controller in the dev cluster; collect microbenchmarks. Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement revocable leases, integrate batch-deflation logic, add metrics (lease_count, lease_revocations, deflation_events, admission_latency_p50/p95/p99). Phase 3 (2 weeks): reconstruction pipeline + client opt-in checkpoint API + fallback micro-model orchestration. Phase 4: canary rollout (10% traffic per region) with automatic rollback on increased error rate or token-cost regression.
metrics_and_sla_targets: Primary metric: reduction in hard OOMs (track OOM kills per 100k requests) target -70% on canary. Latency: p99 tail increase <= 10% during steady-state. Cost: token/compute delta <= +3% on average. Observability: add Grafana dashboard for lease metrics and a Prometheus alert for >10 revocations/min per worker.
test_plan: Unit tests for lease lifecycle, integration tests for admission controller under synthetic memory pressure, e2e load test with mixed sequence lengths and concurrency (use existing perf harness runtime/perf/kv-stress). Run fault-injection where lease revocations trigger reconstruction and measure success rate and latencies. Create a canary job in CI that runs under real traffic patterns for 72h.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off by default. 2) Internal dev cluster testing. 3) Canary on non-prod with 5% traffic for 48h. 4) Canary on prod with a single low-impact customer for 72h. 5) Gradual ramp to 25%, 50%, 100% with monitoring gates. Immediate rollback if OOM rate increases or request error rate > 0.5% or cost regression > 10%.
